# evals/fixtures -- label schema and generator

## What this is

Synthetic, generated fixtures for TASK-TEST-001 (labelled domain datasets:
retail, saas, agriculture) and TASK-TEST-002 (insufficient, ambiguous, messy,
hostile fixtures). No third-party or real data of any kind. No real persons;
all IDs and names are generator-produced (e.g. `C0001`, `Item 3`).

**License note:** synthetic, generated by `scripts/generate_fixtures.py`; no
third-party data; no real persons; free to use/modify within this project.

## How to regenerate

```
python scripts/generate_fixtures.py
```

- Seed: `42` (fixed; see `SEED` constant in the script).
- Stdlib only: `csv, json, random, zipfile, datetime, decimal, pathlib`.
- Deterministic: every dataset is generated from one `random.Random(42)`
  instance in a fixed call order, and all money math uses `decimal.Decimal`
  (never `float`), so re-running reproduces byte-identical files.

### Reproducibility check (two runs, compare SHA-256 of every file)

```
python scripts/generate_fixtures.py
python - <<'PY'
import hashlib, pathlib
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path("evals/fixtures").rglob("*")):
    if p.is_file():
        print(p, hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
PY
```
Run that whole block twice and diff the two outputs -- it must be empty.

## Label schema (`labels.json` in each dataset directory)

```jsonc
{
  "dataset": "<name>",
  "domain": {"expected_status": "known|multi|ambiguous|unknown",
              "primary": "<domain id or null>",
              "acceptable_alternatives": ["..."]},   // design.md Sec 14
  "tables": {
    "<table>": {
      "row_count": 123,
      "columns": {
        "<column>": {"semantic_type": "<TRD 11.2 type>",
                       "role": "identifier|time|measure|dimension",
                       "additivity": "additive|semi_additive|non_additive|n/a",
                       "unit": "currency:INR|count|pct|..."}
      }
    }
  },
  "entities": [{"name": "...", "table": "...", "key": ["..."]}],
  "relationships": [{"from_table": "...", "from_column": "...",
                       "to_table": "...", "to_column": "...", "cardinality": "..."}],
  "kpis": {"<kpi>": {"formula": "<exact formula>", "unit": "...", "values": {...}}},
  "available_analyses": ["..."],
  "unavailable_analyses": [{"analysis": "...", "reason_code": "<TRD 14.2 code>", "message": "..."}],
  "rca_ground_truth": { ... },        // retail only (AC-7)
  "anomaly_ground_truth": [ ... ],      // retail only
  "generator": {"seed": 42, "script": "scripts/generate_fixtures.py"}
}
```

Reason codes follow TRD Sec 14.2: `NO_TIME_DIMENSION`, `IRREGULAR_TIME`,
`INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY`, `NO_RETENTION_HISTORY`. `NO_CUSTOMER_IDENTIFIER` is a
generator-documented extension of that list (same naming convention) used
where a dataset has no customer column at all, which is stronger than
"insufficient history" -- customer-level analyses are structurally
impossible, not just under-powered.

Messy/hostile fixtures use `files.<name>.expected_outcome` (`accept_with_flags`
or `reject`) plus, for rejections, `error_code` / `reason` matching TRD Sec 35
(e.g. `SECURITY_ERROR` / `ZIP_BOMB`, displayed as `SECURITY_ERROR(ZIP_BOMB)`).

## Security note (hostile/)

`evals/fixtures/hostile/README.md` repeats this: those files are inert test
fixtures (a mislabelled XLSX, a macro-enabled XLSM with a placeholder VBA
part, CSV-injection payloads). Never open them with desktop tools; feed them
only to the ingestion pipeline under test. The zip bomb and oversized-file
generators (`make_zip_bomb`, `make_oversized_csv` in
`scripts/generate_fixtures.py`) are NOT committed -- call them from a test at
test time, writing into a tmp directory.
